findings.issue: Module-level promise memoization (speciesPromise/typesPromise/generationsPromise) never clears a rejected promise; api() evicts failures from its cache (api.js:36) but these memos do not, so a single transient API failure makes the home page and every loadSpecies-dependent page render 'Not found' for the rest of the session.
findings.suggestion: Reset the memo in a .catch() (e.g. `speciesPromise = api(...).catch(e => { speciesPromise = null; throw e; })`) so the next navigation retries.

findings.issue: All non-404 errors (network outage, API 500, JSON parse failure) render the 'Not found' page, presenting backend failures as missing resources.
findings.suggestion: Render a distinct error state (e.g. 'Something went wrong') for non-404 failures, with the Not found page reserved for 404s and unrouted paths.

findings.issue: Sorting a moves table replaces the entire panel via outerHTML and re-attaches handlers, dropping focus from the sort button that was clicked/activated — keyboard and screen-reader users lose their place.
findings.suggestion: Re-render only the table body rows in place, or restore focus to the sort button after replacing the panel.

findings.issue: An out-of-range `?page=` (e.g. 999) is clamped for display but the URL is not corrected, so the address bar and pagination links disagree with the rendered page.
findings.suggestion: Replace the history entry with the clamped URL when filters.page exceeds totalPages.

findings.issue: The alternate-form cutoff is inlined as `id >= 10000` instead of reusing the isAlternateFormId helper already exported from api.js and used in data.js.
findings.suggestion: Import and use isAlternateFormId(id) for consistency.

findings.issue: escapeAttr is an exact alias of escapeHtml with no behavioral difference; the name implies a distinction that doesn't exist.
findings.suggestion: Either drop it and use escapeHtml at attribute interpolation sites, or keep it but document that it exists to make call sites self-documenting.

findings.issue: send() writes a body regardless of request method; a HEAD request with a malformed URL hits the 400 path and receives a body, violating HEAD semantics (other HEAD paths are handled correctly).
findings.suggestion: Pass the request method to send() and skip the body for HEAD responses.

findings.issue: responseCache is unbounded; a long session browsing many Pokémon pages accumulates every move/version-group detail. The spec explicitly permits in-memory caching, so this is acceptable, but it will matter if the pattern spreads.
findings.suggestion: Consider a simple LRU cap if the cache footprint grows, or leave as-is with a note that it is bounded by the API's fixed dataset.

findings.issue: renderToken and searchTimer are module-level mutable globals coordinating render staleness and debouncing; correct today, but hidden global state that a second interactive page would need to replicate.
findings.suggestion: If another interactive route is added, fold the token and timers into a small per-navigation render context instead of adding more globals.

summary: A clean, current-Vite vanilla SPA that follows the framework's own scaffold and shows real care in escaping, race guarding, and bounded fetch fan-out. The one thing I'd block on is the never-cleared promise memoization in data.js, which turns a single transient API failure into a session-long 'Not found' on the home page; a distinct error state and a few focus/consistency nits round out the ask. I'd merge after that small round of changes.
